vramtweak.gui.title: VRAM Tweak
vramtweak.gui.restartRequired: §cYou must restart your game to change the VRAM Optimization state.
vramtweak.gui.restartRequired.title: §c§lConfirm VRAM Optimization Change
vramtweak.gui.restartRequired.message: §cVRAM Optimization state has changed!§7This option requires §ea game restart §7to take effect.§7Loaded textures will not be dynamically restored.§cAre you sure you want to change this?
vramtweak.gui.option.vram.enabled.toolti:
Master switch. When off, no VRAM optimizations apply.
This option change will take effect the next time you launch the game—this mod intercepts texture creation, and loaded textures will not be dynamically restored.
vramtweak.gui.option.formatDownscale.too:
Requires "VRAM Optimization" master switch ON.
RGBA16F → RGBA8, saves ~50% VRAM on color targets.
Available when high-precision formats exist (26.2+).
vramtweak.gui.option.depthDownscale.tool:
Requires "VRAM Optimization" master switch ON.
D32 → D16, saves ~50% VRAM per shadow map.
vramtweak.gui.option.budgetTracking.tool:
Requires "VRAM Optimization" master switch ON.
Monitors VRAM usage in real-time. Logs warnings when exceeding threshold.
vramtweak.gui.option.budgetWarningPercen:
Requires "VRAM Optimization" master switch ON.
Triggers warning when VRAM usage exceeds this % (50–95).
▲ Higher = warns only when closer to limit.
▼ Lower = earlier warning, more time to react.
Default 80%.
vramtweak.gui.option.atlasSizeLimit.tool:
When on, caps block/item texture atlas resolution.
HD packs with 8192px+ atlases use significant VRAM.
Verified: blocks.png 16384→4096 saves ~240MB.
Use with 'Max Atlas Size' setting.
vramtweak.gui.option.maxAtlasSize.toolti:
Texture atlas resolution cap (1024–16384). Caps oversized.
▲ Higher = sharper textures, single atlas may use 240+ MB.
▼ Lower = saves VRAM significantly, minimal blur at 4096.
Default 4096.
vramtweak.gui.option.governor.enabled.to:
Auto-lowers render distance under VRAM pressure → frees VRAM.
Restores stepwise when safe → minimal impact on experience.
 The reduction is dynamic and temporary — check the HUD for actual effective render distance, the settings menu still shows your configured value.
Use with Hysteresis / Min Distance / Cooldown settings.
vramtweak.gui.option.hysteresis.tooltip:
Buffer zone for restoring render distance (2–30).
VRAM must fall below (threshold − hysteresis) to recover.
▲ Higher = more stable, no frequent switching, slower recovery.
▼ Lower = faster recovery, may oscillate.
Default 10%.
vramtweak.gui.option.minDistance.tooltip:
Lower bound for governor render distance (2–16).
▲ Higher = more distant terrain visible, less VRAM saving.
▼ Lower = more VRAM saved under pressure, less visible terrain.
Default 4.
vramtweak.gui.option.cooldownTicks.toolt:
Minimum interval between governor changes (20–600 ticks).
▲ Higher = smoother transitions, slower response.
▼ Lower = faster reaction, render distance may change rapidly.
Default 100 ticks (5 seconds).
vramtweak.gui.option.verificationLog.too:
Logs before→after for every optimization intervention.
Output to latest.log, prefix [VRAM-Tweak Verify].
Use grep to check if mod is active.
Recommended only when troubleshooting.
vramtweak.gui.option.hud.enabled.tooltip: Real-time FPS / VRAM / frame time overlay.
vramtweak.gui.option.showFps1Percent.too: Slowest 1% frames — key perceived smoothness metric.
vramtweak.gui.option.showAtlas.tooltip: Shows tracked atlas count and cap triggers.
vramtweak.gui.option.showDownscales.tool: Shows D32→D16 depth and format downscale triggers.
vramtweak.gui.option.showBudget.tooltip: Shows VRAM budget alert status and peak usage.
vramtweak.gui.option.allocTracker.toolti:
Intercepts every GPU texture allocation/deallocation at the OpenGL level.
Tracks which subsystem created each texture, categorized by type and source.
Useful for diagnosing what fills VRAM. Takes effect immediately — no restart.
 Performance: negligible overhead when off; when on, some per-allocation cost.
vramtweak.gui.option.allocSnapshotInterv:
How often (in seconds) to print an aggregated allocation summary to the log.
Shorter = more frequent reports; longer = less log noise.
Default 30s.
Show VRAM breakdown by category on the HUD.
Requires AllocTracker to be enabled.
Example: VRAM: 4.5/8.0GB [Tex:3.0GB RT:1.5GB]

vramtweak.gui.option.showVoxy.tooltip: Shows Voxy's own tracked VRAM: LOD mesh buffers + immutable textures.
vramtweak.gui.option.voxy.enabled.toolti:
Voxy pre-allocates ~4GB of GPU geometry buffer that stays fully resident in VRAM.
Caps it via the official 'voxy.geometryBufferSizeOverrideMB' system property.
Saves up to ~3GB VRAM on 8GB cards; far LOD unloads sooner.
Takes effect when you enter a world (re-enter the current world to apply).
vramtweak.gui.option.voxy.limitMB.toolti:
Max Voxy geometry buffer in MB (1024–4096).
1024 ≈ 1GB (recommended for 8GB cards).
Values below 1024 can thrash Voxy's node hierarchy and balloon VRAM — the mod clamps them to 1024.
Only applies when the Limit toggle is on.
vramtweak.gui.option.showGovernor.toolti: Shows VRAM governor auto-adjust status and current render distance cap.
